description: Unauthorized GitHub Workflow Trigger Attackers can create pull requests or comment on existing PRs to trigger workflow runs. If not properly configured, forked repositories can also trigger workflows with access to secrets. An attacker forks the repository, modifies the workflow to exfiltrate secrets, and creates a PR to trigger the malicious workflow.
references: recommendation: Implement strict GitHub workflow trigger controls

description: Container Image Vulnerabilities Vulnerable container images may contain known CVEs in base images, application dependencies, or system packages that could be exploited once deployed. An attacker exploits a known vulnerability in an outdated package within the deployed container to achieve remote code execution.
references: recommendation: Implement container image scanning and policy enforcement
recommendation: Implement runtime container security controls

description: Secrets and Configuration Exposure Secrets can be exposed through committed code, environment variables in logs, or misconfigured access policies to AWS Secrets Manager. An attacker finds AWS credentials in Git history or CloudWatch logs, using them to access AWS resources.
references: recommendation: Prevent secrets exposure in logs and code

description: DDoS and Resource Exhaustion Attackers can generate high volumes of traffic to trigger App Runner auto-scaling, leading to increased costs and potential service disruption. An attacker launches a DDoS attack causing App Runner to scale up significantly, resulting in unexpected costs.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1498 - Network Denial of Service

description: VPC Network Security Misconfigurations Overly permissive security groups, misconfigured route tables, or improperly configured network ACLs can expose services to unauthorized access. An attacker exploits overly permissive security group rules to access internal services that should not be exposed.
references: recommendation: Implement network monitoring and alerting

description: IAM Role and Permission Misconfigurations Overly permissive IAM roles or policies can allow services or users to access resources beyond their intended scope. An attacker exploits an overly permissive App Runner instance role to access sensitive data in other AWS services.

DNS-Based Attacks Attackers can exploit DNS misconfigurations for zone enumeration, cache poisoning, or denial of service attacks. An attacker performs DNS zone walking to enumerate subdomains and identify potential targets.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1071.004 - Application Layer Protocol: DNS
recommendation: Implement DNS monitoring and alerting
